items.title: Flight recorders recovered from 'devastating' Amazon cargo plane crash
items.description: Five people were killed and five others seriously injured when the Boeing 767-300 overshot the runway at Miami International Airport.

items.title: Palestinian parents fear for children's lives at school as settler attacks grow
items.description: A headteacher in the occupied West Bank has installed new barbed wire fencing after three pupils were killed this year.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD says 'democracy demands' parties work with them after state election win
items.description: The far-right party is trying to form a government in the state after falling three seats short of a majority.

items.title: Eiffel Tower shut by staff protest after female workers moved for religious visit
items.description: The mayor of Paris said an investigation would be launched into the incident, which left female employees "humiliated", according to a union representative.

items.title: Ukraine's chief prosecutor resigns over call centre corruption scandal
items.description: In his resignation letter, Ruslan Kravchenko denied the allegations against him, saying he did not want his office "to be used as a tool in political confrontation".

items.title: UK government expected to announce restrictions on trade with West Bank settlements
items.description: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is set to outline the proposals today, in a move which could prompt Israel to retaliate.

items.title: Trump threatens to stop sale of Canadian Bombardier jets in US
items.description: The threat against one of Canada's largest companies comes amid an escalating trade war between the two neighbours.

items.title: North Korea and Russia open first road bridge linking both countries
items.description: It comes as relations between both countries have strengthened since the start of the Ukraine war.

items.title: Trial over alleged murders of Australian surfer brothers starts in Mexico
items.description: The bodies of Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend were found with gunshot wounds to their heads.

items.title: Thousands turn out in Serbia for funeral of 'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladić
items.description: Mladić was jailed for genocide during the 1990s Bosnian war and the EU warned Serbia not to glorify the convicted war criminal.

items.title: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanese village kill 12
items.description: Lebanon says a recent Israeli escalation is jeopardising a US-brokered ceasefire meant to end the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

items.title: Grindr to pay £26m to settle claims it allegedly shared users' HIV status
items.description: The long-running claim alleges Grindr breached UK privacy laws by sharing data with third parties.

items.title: Nepal observes national day of mourning for victims of flash flood disaster
items.description: Flags flew at half mast on the 13th day since the disaster, the last day of the Hindu mourning period.

items.title: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes
items.description: Schools, businesses and public transport are all struggling with the surge in Russian air attacks.

items.title: A food safety officer has become a social media star in India - why?
items.description: Tukaram Mundhe has gone viral after a series of aggressive inspections of restaurants to detect hygiene lapses.

items.title: AI cancer cures slowed by chip shortage, says UK's biggest tech boss
items.description: The head of chip designer Arm says modelling how a DNA marker is impacted by cancer cannot be done now, but computers are "going to solve it".

items.title: New videos of man in 9/11 lawsuit reveal extremist links
items.description: The footage and other evidence the FBI failed to share undermine Omar al-Bayoumi's 25 years of denials.

items.title: How significant are AfD's historic gains for Germany and the rest of Europe?
items.description: The BBC's Europe editor Katya Adler sees the far-right win in Saxony-Anhalt state ringing alarm bells for the EU and traditional parties.

items.title: Peace talks rich in symbolism but fundamental differences between Russia and Ukraine remain
items.description: Despite talks between US envoys and both Putin and Zelensky, the expectation in Kyiv is the fighting will continue, writes James Landale.

items.title: How £725 game-show winnings kick-started Champions League coach's career
items.description: Lithuanian coach Valdas Dambrauskas cut his teeth in English football, and now returns in the Champions League with Sabah.
